scope: Complete JVM client requirement in GOAL.md, within all 450 capabilities and 41 families; this plan removes no other work.

qualified_gradle.limits: Named publication-wire-v2 cases only; full JVM and Maven parity remain unfinished.

execution_order: Ant/Ivy release publication and transitive consumption on each native Linux architecture
Ivy snapshot, classifier, parent, dynamic and conflict cases; controlled interruption and recovery
SBT 2.x plus supported 1.x publisher/consumer workflows with isolated project dependency caches
Production TLS/private CA, independent hosts, faults, lifecycle, migration, scale and every remaining JVM requirement

ivy.state: Both native419861cAnt identities repaired; first publication fails unsupported sha256 spelling. Configuration/parent-checksum repairs and three SHA-2 consumers implemented but replay unverified.
mechanism: Install hash-verified official distributions only on isolated native GitHub hosts; pin the actual JDK/runtime and all tool, fixture and source bytes.
Run only project-owned Ant build XML and bundled Ivy Ant tasks. Generate resource-only JARs and POMs with ivy:makepom. Never run resolved package code.
Publish through a Maven-compatible URL resolver with HTTP PUT and publishivy=false; ibiblio explicitly does not support publishing.

Resolve through ibiblio with m2compatible=true and usepoms=true at one explicit cratectl endpoint. Use a fresh cache per attempt, credentials bound to host/realm cratectl and no implicit Maven Central fallback.
Bind every published JAR/POM to its exact retained path, digest and size, then independently read HTTP bytes. The generated Ivy-to-POM mapping must preserve the expected dependency graph.
first_required_cases: scoped writer publishes a dependency and two application versions
review blocks metadata and JAR before a decision
exact JAR/POM readback and complete transitive dependency set
colliding coordinates in two isolated tenants
proxy checksum validation and group member precedence
actual registry restart and fresh resolution
revoked writer and reader denials with the other tenant unaffected
later_mandatory_cases: timestamped and nonunique Maven snapshots under explicit redeployment policy
parent POMs, classifiers, configuration mapping, exclusions and conflict resolution
concurrent publish, interrupted transfer/retry, conditional cache and upstream outage
deletion/restore, lifecycle and complete permission, source, failure and scale combinations
ivy.toolchain: Apache Ant 1.10.18 and Apache Ivy 2.6.0; exact official URLs/checksums are in runtime_pins.

sbt.state: planned; no SBT installation, execution or compatibility pass
sbt.next: Pin official distribution checksums and review current 2.x/1.x configuration contracts before implementation. Preserve independent client/version cases.
mechanism: Separate stock SBT/tool boot dependency bootstrap from the product journey; record actual bootstrap identities and external fetch limits.
Use only owned build definitions and resource-only published JARs. Disable Scala artifact cross names where appropriate. Never execute resolved package code.

Use one explicit cratectl source for project dependencies and fresh project artifact caches. Warm boot caches must not contain owned fixture coordinates; fallback or preseeded fixtures cannot stand in for an observed registry resolution.

Actual publication/consumption, transitive dependency bytes, current policy/authorization, proxy/groups, snapshots, tenant collisions, restart, revocation and later lifecycle/fault cases are mandatory.

placement.local: Small Python/HTTP stand-ins for bounded mapping, configuration, privacy and failure classification; no emulation or local real JVM/PostgreSQL campaign.
placement.native_ci: Separate native Linux amd64/arm64 jobs with fail-fast=false; real PostgreSQL 16.15 and a nonowner, nonsuperuser runtime without BYPASSRLS; owned loopback ports 35432/38443; explicit job/client time, memory and output limits.
placement.evidence: Reviewed bounded fields, counts, digests and stages only. Each client/version has its own mandatory profile. Preserve original failures; partial, skipped or absent cases never pass.
placement.limits: Owned POSIX process-group cleanup does not prove control of processes that explicitly detach into new sessions. Qualify client fork settings and runner containment before stronger descendant claims.
